Introduction #

Welcome to my personal website!

I am a PhD student in Astrophysics at the University of California San Diego and an LSST Data Science Fellow. I’m interested in pursuing projects applying computational methods onto fundamental Astrophysics. My current work focuses on galaxy and dark matter simulations.

Outside of research, I am determined to uplift emerging scientists and lower the barrier to theoretical sciences.

Feel free to look around, explore my research and art sections, or access my contact information and CV here.

Research Interests #

I have done a wide array of research projects in different fields of astrophysics. My research section details those works. Here is a brief synopsis:

Computational Astrophysics #

  • Hydrodynamical simulations
  • Semi-Analytical models
  • Structure formation
  • Numerical methods

Cosmology #

  • Near Field Cosmology
  • Reionization
  • High-z dwarf galaxies
  • Dark Matter & energy
  • CMB

Topical Interests #

  • Local Group
  • Strong lensing
  • Ultra-faint dwarfs
  • Stellar streams
  • Baryonic & dark sector physics

Other Interests #

In my free time, I enjoying traveling, hiking, and photographing the world. I’ve taken up running and ultimate. I read occassionally with a focus on forgotten historical periods, and my favorite author is George Eliot. I also take interest in philosophies of Nietzsche. I am additionally an avid gamer with a focus on indie games.

Background #

I am natively from Beijing, China. I was selected into the Zaopei program of the RDFZ middle school, where I developed an interest in science and specifically astronomy. I subsequently went to the United States for high school, and spent my formative years in Pittsburgh. After graduating from Shady Side Academy with a Summa Cum Laude, I attended the University of Chicago with a B.S. in Astrophysics and graduating with honors. I now pursue a Ph.D. in Astrophysics at the University of California San Diego with PI Ethan Nadler as an LSST Data Science Fellow.
